english.title: Set snare to cause injury to wild animal
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) set in position a self-locking snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(1)(a) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) Section 48 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 amends the extent of this offence so it no longer applies in Wales after the 16th October 2023. For the offence applying in England from this date, see H101416. See H101437 for a similar offence in Wales.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant set in position a self-locking snare which was of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to any wild animal coming into contact with it.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates Court was removed - as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date was unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
